chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ma'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"There is no li'an (oath of imprecation) until he claims that he has personally seen (the act)."

key_terms.عَايَنَ: He personally witnessed or saw with his own eyes
key_terms.لِعَانٌ: Li'an, the oath of imprecation between husband and wife in case of adultery accusation

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for li'an to be valid according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural requirement for *li'an*, specifying that the husband must assert personal eyewitness (*mu'ayana*) of the act, distinguishing it from general knowledge or hearsay. This emphasis on direct observation underscores the gravity of the oath and the high evidentiary threshold required to establish the specific charge of adultery in Shia jurisprudence. It serves as a critical interpretive key for understanding the application of Surah An-Nur's provisions regarding marital discord and proof.
